card.title: MicroFire
card.body: The Living Science Observatory: NASA's microgravity fire evidence, checked at the source.
card.foot: Team MicroFire · Independent project, not NASA-endorsed

shots.caption: We're Team MicroFire. We love space, and we wanted fire science anyone can check.
Gravity changes a flame. Switch it on and off in the Gravity Lens, with PIX as your guide.
We built one place where students, teachers and researchers meet the real evidence.

card.title: The evidence is real. It is also buried.
card.body: NASA has flown fire experiments in microgravity. Their results sit in long technical reports, and copied catalogs drift from the source.

shots.caption: On Earth, hot gas rises. In microgravity it can't, so a flame behaves differently. Space fire safety needs its own evidence.
Our Atlas admits only records checked against the NASA source: 1 admitted, 55 quarantined until verified.
BASS-II test B20: a PMMA film burning against airflow, documented in one NASA report.
A copied catalog said 16.5% oxygen. NASA Table A.1, page 112, says 17.4% calibrated. We fixed it.
Missing values stay 'not recorded'. Nothing is filled in by guesswork.
Future crews need to know what was measured, and what is still unknown.

card.title: A research observatory that shows its work.
card.body: Search, trace, ask and export. Every answer carries its NASA page and its limits.

shots.caption: Ask PIX answers from cited evidence only. No AI model: every line links to its page.
Ask beyond the evidence and PIX says so instead of guessing.
At a glance: what NASA recorded, what matches your question, what differs, and the key limit.
The Citation Checker confirms a reference against the NASA source and flags a wrong page.
The B20 dossier explains the instrument part by part. Unknown values stay 'not recorded'.
Evidence exports keep their sources and limitations.

card.title: Learn by doing the science.
card.body: Five missions turn the evidence into play. They are designed and the rules are tested; none is playable yet.

shots.caption: From station arrival to a fictional lunar habitat, each decision will cite its evidence.
Mission 05 asks what NASA evidence can and cannot tell a habitat designer.
The BASS-II training bay is built in 3D. Its gameplay opens after server integration.

card.title: What works today, and what doesn't yet
card.body: Working: the Atlas, the B20 dossier, cited Ask PIX, the evidence trace and export. Not yet: playable missions, more admitted records, independent science review.

card.title: Where we go from here
card.body: Verify more NASA records · connect the mission server · independent science review · test with students and teachers.

card.title: Help us grow the evidence
card.body: Combustion-science reviewers, time with more NASA reports, and classrooms willing to test.
